label: Person
name: Adrianus Djajasepoetra
summary:
Adrianus Djajasepoetra SJ (1914–1979) was an Indonesian Jesuit bishop who served as Archbishop of Semarang in Java, one of the most significant Catholic sees in Southeast Asia. Born in Java under Dutch colonial rule, he was ordained a Jesuit priest and was one of the first indigenous Indonesians to reach episcopal leadership in the rapidly developing Indonesian Catholic Church.

Djajasepoetra's episcopate coincided with Indonesia's Sukarno and early Suharto eras, a period of intense political turbulence that included the 1965–1966 mass killings following the Communist coup attempt, when hundreds of thousands of Indonesians were killed. The Catholic Church in Indonesia—a small minority in the world's largest Muslim country—navigated these upheavals with caution, seeking to protect its institutions and communities without political alignment.

As an indigenous Indonesian archbishop, Djajasepoetra represented a crucial transition in Indonesian Catholicism from Dutch missionary domination to locally led Church. The Jesuit presence in Java included distinguished figures like van Lith who had established the distinctive Javanese Catholic culture that Djajasepoetra inherited and developed. His leadership helped establish Indonesian Catholic identity as genuinely indigenous rather than a colonial import.
